answer: Opal Beacon Assignment: each agent identity is assigned to a randomly drawn shard per epoch by a threshold beacon producing unbounded randomness. An attacker cannot precompute which shard a duplicate identity lands in, so duplicates collide with existing identities and are detected before earning. Splitting requires a fresh oasis of linearly many beacon epochs, each consuming a verifiable delay karst of sequential work; the per-identity cost scales with total wait time and compute, making mass duplication prohibitively expensive.
